Hi Luis / Evergreen ops team,

Great to kick off this private deployment intake. I’m Aisha (Enterprise Solutions at Redwood Inference) and I’ll be the primary contact for environment coordination. I’ve looped Ben (Onboarding PM) and Kimberly (Network Engineer) to capture technical prerequisites.

Goal for this thread: align on the minimal items we need to validate before we schedule the tenant provisioning window — network ranges, egress routes, KMS access model, and a short environments checklist we can use for a smoke run.

Ask for today: can you send the public egress IP ranges and confirm whether the tenant will sit in a dedicated VPC or within an existing VPC (and the expected project/account IDs)? If you have an internal contact for KMS/HSM or procurement edge, please CC them.

I’ve attached a short intake template (Launchpad intake) and a one-page network requirements summary to make this easier to share with your infra team.

Proposed follow-ups:
- You send IP ranges + VPC choice by Thu 9/9
- Redwood to return a pre-configured routing checklist and a proposed provisioning window by Mon 9/13

Thanks — looking forward to working with you.

Best,

Thanks, all. Short answers and a checklist to make the handoff concrete — I’ve pasted the key validation items below and attached a filled example of the intake template.

Network & infra minimums (validation items):
1) VPC design:
   - Dedicated VPC (proj-prod-eh) with two subnets: control (10.40.10.0/24) and worker (10.40.20.0/22).
   - Route tables configured so workers egress via NAT to the provided public prefixes.
2) Firewall / allowlist:
   - Outbound allowlist: 52.45.20.0/24, 18.204.33.0/24 (plus any additional outbound CIDRs you provide).
   - Inbound: only RBAC/API ports from our control-plane peering (we will share port list in the attached PDF).
3) Service account & IAM:
   - Create a service account: redwood-deploy-egh@proj-prod-eh with roles: compute.viewer, network.viewer, kms.cryptoDecrypter (if customer-KMS mode), and storage.objectViewer. No owner-level roles.
4) KMS mode options (pick one):
   - Customer-managed KMS: provide an IAM binding that allows the Redwood service account to use the key for decrypt operations; we will not store keys.
   - Redwood-managed key with external audit: Redwood will provision a key in our account and provide audit logs and export receipts.
5) DNS & FQDN:
   - Provide a short-lived DNS name for smoke-tests or a private zone entry.
6) Temporary access for validation:
   - Either a temporary SSH bastion (us-east-1 jump host) or we can run agentless tests from your API endpoints if you prefer no bastion.

Smoke-run test plan (summary):
- Redwood provisions tenant resources (30-45 min)
- Connectivity checks: route table egress, NAT translation, KMS key usage test (10 min)
- Model inference smoke: run 100 small requests to validate latency/kv-cache behavior (10 min)
- Telemetry and logs check: ensure metrics are reaching your monitoring stack and our control-plane ingestion (10 min)

Attachments in this message: filled Launchpad intake (20260907-launchpad-intake-template.xlsx), network-requirements-summary.pdf.

If customer KMS is the choice, Luis please cc the security/KMS engineer so we can validate the IAM statement. If you prefer the Redwood-managed flow we can proceed without a customer KMS IAM binding but will need an approval from procurement for the key-handling agreement.

— Kimberly
Senior Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
